media.caption: The episode you double-click heads Jedi Knight's list
Gobinator: double-click a Jedi Knight episode and play it

feed.text: Gobinator, the double-click launcher for Jedi Knight episode GOBs, was picked back up. Its 2022 version builds again and was put through ten test scenarios, which showed fourteen flaws, the worst a cleanup that could delete a player's own GOBs.

The new Gobinator removes only the episodes it copied in itself, starts the game without a batch file, handles accented and Japanese file names, says what went wrong when something fails, and recognises Steam, GOG, community, JK Remastered and OpenJKDF2 installs.
On OpenJKDF2 v0.9.9, one double-click on an episode GOB now drops the player straight into its first level, with no menus in between.

Gobinator now puts the episode you double-click at the top of Jedi Knight's episode list, past the game's 64-episode limit, using an empty folder of the same name beside it. Your own mods still load on top, and starting Gobinator by itself brings back the usual list.

On JK Remastered 3.3 a double-click now goes straight into an episode's first level with no clicks, and the GOG release of Jedi Knight works too. Older OpenJKDF2 builds that can't start a level directly now open at their menu instead of quitting.
Gobinator now spots a Steam copy of Jedi Knight that Steam would never actually start, and names the folder Steam does start, instead of copying the episode somewhere the game can't see it.

Gobinator got its own look: a rusted-steel G firing an amber play arrow as its icon, now built into the program, a GOBINATOR wordmark, key art of a hangar door opening onto a desert canyon, and real screenshots of it at work, ready for its listing on the studio's site.

On OpenJKDF2, Gobinator now tells single-player episodes from multiplayer ones: single player lands in the first level, and multiplayer hosts a game on your PC with you in it. A mod, or a GOB it cannot read, is left where it is and the game opens at its menu.

Gobinator can now be unzipped anywhere: the first time it finds no game beside it, it asks where Jedi Knight is and remembers the answer. A missing settings file is written with the defaults, so a bare gobinator.exe is a complete install.

Gobinator's new look is a terminal line, > GOBINATOR_ in glowing amber phosphor, picked from a sheet of twelve directions, with a matching GOB icon on a small CRT screen. The key art and the screenshots stayed.

Gobinator 1.1 is out, public domain, source on GitHub: double-click a Jedi Knight episode and the game starts with it first in its list, on OpenJKDF2, JK Remastered and the Steam, GOG and CD releases. Proven on an install with 141 episodes, past the game's 64-episode limit.

Gobinator's guide to signing a Windows release, shared with the studio's other projects, was checked and corrected: the free signing service for open-source projects takes only OSI-approved licences, which public-domain CC0 is not, and certificates now last at most 15 months.
